I should probably start by declaring my interest in the Elder Scolls games, from Morrowind to Skyrim I've plowed hours into these games and have some great memories, therefore when I first heard that ESO was coming out I was ecstatic....Furthermore I am currently only level 25 after plowing around 50 hours in to the game therefore I will add some more in the comments as I venture through Tamriel. Now for the review

Controls: I think the controls are near to perfect for an xbox mmo, there are hundreds of different button combos that you could set up, and all things considered it never feels to complicated or to simple. Any one familiar with Skyrim should be able to pick it up quite easily

Map: This is probably the most disappointing aspect of Tamriel Unlimited, the fact that you can't travel everywhere yet is a big negative in my book. I can't help feel that it hinders the immersion in the world that was so epic in Skyrim and of which can still be done in other mmo's such as WoW

Guilds and Community: Once again I can't help but compare the Tamriel online community to that of other mmorpgs that I have played most notably WoW. The microphone thing works ok in big cities but can get incredibly annoying if someone's mic has broken and It just seems like a pain to have to jump through so many hoops to change to your guild chat and then back to area then to group (especially if you are in 3 guilds). Furthermore the guilds seem to be less community organized than guilds that i'm used to on PC mmo's, I'm not sure if this is because it's a console game and therefore attracts a different type of community or because you are allowed to join 3 different guilds and therefore you lose your close connection to just one guild.

Quests and story line: I've enjoyed the quests so far it is not close to being as big a grind as some console "mmo" such as Destiny (I know they claim Destiny isn't an MMO as) however the main story line seems to get lost in the vast array of quests that you will be doing. once again this didn't cause me much worry because there's plenty of lore to get yourself lost in

Dungeons: Probably some of the most fun dungeons I have done on any game so far. Although the group finder is far from perfect it still does the job (70% of the time!)

Graphics: This is probably the most disapointing aspect of the game for me. Don't get me wrong there is nothing bad about the graphics however for some reason I'm yet to get that AAAA WAAWWW look at that feeling which I had consistently with Skyrim

One final note: There are only a fraction of the chests in Tamriel compared to Skyrim just one more thing that Skyrim fans might find disappointing when making the switch

Overall my experience of the game has been very good and I have really enjoyed it, however it simply can't hold up to the incredibly high bar that was set by Skyrim and to an extent it shouldn't even try because it is a great game that's trying to take the franchise to a new areas (as long as that area is Tamriel :P)
REVIEW: Elder Scolls Tamriel Unlimited, (Xbox One version)
